newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Horn denies minister mulling resignation.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Horn denies minister mulling resignation.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn denied on Thursday that Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy had threatened to resign over concessions to protesting farmers which would dilute his economic programme.
"(Medgyessy) did not hold out the prospect of resigning," Horn was quoted as saying by Hungarian television.
Farmers from central Hungary's Kiskoros region have set up roadblocks since February 24 protesting that taxes are too high and demanding they be exempt from social security contributions.
On Wednesday they failed to show up at a meeting with Horn and Medgyessy after which Horn said negotiations were off.
"The government regards the talks as finished," he told reporters.
Medgyessy said he would remain in his post as long as no concessions were made to "preferred social sectors".
He added regular employees still pay twice as much tax as farmers and that he would not agree to regulations that would result in unequal burdens.
"I am unwilling to agree to any substantial change affecting the proportionate sharing of tax burdens," Medgyessy said.
The statement came only days after the minister urged the government and social groups to agree to a programme to slash inflation and curb wage growth in 1998.
The comments apparently contradicted Horn who had earlier played down the importance of wage rises in generating inflation.
